quest.title: Sea Breeze Rendezvous
quest.description: After discussing the plan with Lyney and the others, you go to the seaside to meet The Knave in an attempt to distract her...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Go to the seaside to look for The Knave

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's The Knave! And... Childe!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, aren't you supposed to be in Snezhnaya recuperating? What are you still doing in Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two. I didn't expect to run into you here... *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: I was unconscious for quite a while after the fight in the Primordial Sea. After I woke up, I realized I was being taken back to Snezhnaya, and well...

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: I couldn't have that, now could I? Not when I've still got unfinished business here in Fontaine. So, I mustered up all my strength and made the journey back on my own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What sort of unfinished business are we talking here?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: It has to do with Skirk... My master. I really wanted to meet up with her... But, by the time I got back, she had already left.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: I still have so many questions for her. Without any other leads... all I could do was ask The Knave to help me track her down. She must have left behind some traces from her time in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, okay... So, have you found any clues?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, no. While the House of the Hearth is adept at collecting all manner of intelligence, certain existences... can still manage to escape our purview.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Basically, unless Master feels there's a need to meet with me, she's not going to be found.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: But, that problem has an easy fix. I just need to become stronger, and then... *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon thinks you should focus on getting better first.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Haha, the worst of it is over.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to that one kid from the House of the Hearth... Heloir I think her name was. She gave me a bunch of random potions to drink. They didn't go down easy, let me tell you — pain and chills all over. But, they really did help speed up my recovery.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: And that's good, because it looks like I really do have to head back this time. The old man's been putting the pressure on me. He sent someone to tell me I'm needed for some sort of project...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: "Project Stuzha"?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's the one. *sigh* I heard Regrator's involved too. I'm not looking forward to having to listen to all his monologuing, that's for sure. Hey, maybe you could think of a way for me to stay in Fontaine for a little longer?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Helping Lyney and the others brush up on their fighting skills would be far more interesting. If you and I could spar — that would be even better. I've been waiting for the chance to see you go all out.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: And what a sweet, little daydream that is. But, I also have a role to play in all this. I'll be leaving Fontaine shortly as well.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Besides, considering how little they see fit to step outside the homeland, being called on to return to Snezhnaya by such illustrious dignitaries... What a great "honor," wouldn't you agree?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Haha... One I could do without, I'd say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it just Paimon? Or, does it kinda seem like they're...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just casually trash-talking their colleagues behind their backs...?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: So, dear guests of the House of the Hearth, to what do I owe the visit?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Well, we just, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wanted to learn more about you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! We're super close to Lyney and the others, but we still don't know much about you!

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Is that so? Introductions have already been made, have they not?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, well, you see... There's only so much you can learn about someone from a short introduction! At least tell us something a little extra, like... Why do you call yourself "Father"?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Ooh, good question! I'd also like to know.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The fact that you have to ask tells me our intelligence work has been quite successful. Telling you the answer to that question would only serve to undermine that success, and we can't have that, now can we?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Spoken like a true diplomat. That was some expert sidestepping right there.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Well, if there's nothing else, I think I'll take my leave. I still have a small matter to resolve at home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Wait! Don't go!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If The Knave leaves right now, she's sure to run into Lyney and Clervie...!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Should I release the bird Lyney gave us? No, we should try to get her talking about something else first.)

choices.text: About the House of the Hearth...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Oho, I'd also like to hear the answer to this.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: I've met some of the members of your organization, and they all seemed like really good kids. They actually reminded me of Tonia and Teucer.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Which, by the way, if you ever betray them, I'm just letting you know — I won't let you off easy.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: And why would I betray them?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Well, you've already betrayed the House of the Hearth once, haven't you? At least... that's what I heard.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Okay, okay. I admit, that's just what the old man told me... The Rooster, I mean.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Knave betrayed the House of the Hearth... So, does that mean what Clervie said was true? Does The Knave really treat her children like test subjects?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Wait... did you really do something bad to those kids?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Never mind what I've done, I'm more curious as to what the mighty Rooster had to say. Care to enlighten me?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Ah, well, nothing much... Just some stuff about you taking out many other members of the House of the Hearth, and even going so far as to attack your own "family."

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Hmm... I see.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Based on your reaction, I'm guessing it's all a bunch of lies?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Hardly. I don't appreciate his particular turns of phrase, but I suppose he didn't say anything untrue.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Although, it would be more accurate to say that there is a certain level of prejudice involved... But, I don't intend to clear that up just yet. Prejudice has a funny way of concealing the real truth behind certain things — an attribute that I find to be quite advantageous.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Call yourself a Fontainian, for example, and people will assume all sorts of things, when the real truth... is that this is simply the land where I was raised.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? You're not actually from Fontaine!? But then, why did you try to help out with the prophecy and everything?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I was trying to protect the children born in Fontaine. Claiming that I, myself, was a Fontainian simply made it easier to operate. People would hardly suspect a fellow Fontainian of having any ulterior motives. Who wouldn't want to save their homeland, after all?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: The Primordial Sea wouldn't have any effect on me, but it would have caused great harm to the House of the Hearth... Well, you wanted "extra information," didn't you? There you go. I hope that satisfied your curiosity.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So much for learning anything else about her "betrayal." She probably only revealed that other secret in order to change the subject. It seems like she's trying to avoid talking about her past...)

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: So, you stayed in Fontaine for the kids... I guess I was wrong to believe you'd betray them. Apologies. Looks like I was holding on to some prejudices myself.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Good. Like I said — I like it when others have misconceptions of me.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Actually, while I was recuperating at the House of the Hearth, there was something else that really caught my attention.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: I heard that members always resolve disputes and arguments with a friendly spar, and the loser has to back down. Seems pretty cool, if you ask me. Would also give them plenty of opportunities to hone their skills.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Well, that's only a recent development. In the past, such spars weren't nearly so... friendly. The losing party would lose everything, including their life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They were that high stakes!? Phew, at least that's not a thing anymore!

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Well, the current atmosphere's not half bad. I'm a bit jealous, actually. You've got so many family members around you, and you even get to live with them.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Having a lot of family around means dealing with a considerable amount of bickering and scheming. Once Tonia and Teucer enter their rebellious phase, I'm sure you'll understand.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Just imagine... Teucer becomes obsessed with plucking out strands from the Rooster's mustache, or Tonia decides to dye her hair 42 different colors...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Okay, okay! I get the picture.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: As the conversation shifts to the topic of Tonia and Teucer, Childe begins to share story after story about his siblings.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: It's the type of conversation that would usually leave you falling asleep, but you find yourself grateful to Childe for buying you more time.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Ah, well, would you look at the time. I should probably get going.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, I'm not sure where our paths will cross next, but the next time we run into each other, we should definitely try and find some time to spar... *coughing*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Again, maybe this is a conversation we can have when you look less like you're gonna keel over...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Alright, alright... Well, thanks for everything, Arlecchino.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: No thanks necessary. You also played a part in obtaining the Gnosis. I would say we can call ourselves even.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Hah, I like the sound of that... Well, I'm off. See you all some other time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should probably get going too... Do you wanna head back with us?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Oh? You want me to leave so soon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh... Well, you see, um...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I'm rather enjoying the evening breeze. If you don't mind, I think I'll stick around for a bit. I have some things to think about.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Apologies for not attending to you like a proper host. Please, forgive the slight. I do hope you'll have a pleasant stay.

choices.text: What does the organization mean to you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney! How'd everything go?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, long story short, we ran into a small issue — Clervie can't go into the sunlight.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Everything was fine at first. She followed me up to the surface, just like I told her.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But as I led her out of the shadows and into the sunlight, she vanished.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I turned around, and there she was — standing at the edge of the shadows, silently watching me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe she's afraid of sunlight, or... No, it wouldn't be her wish if that were the case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we could always try... pushing her into it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not sure "pushing" works on a non-corporeal being...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, true...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I've pretty much tried it all already. Nothing worked. Eventually, the sun went down, so all I could do was bring her back here.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: How did it go with you, Lynette?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Good. I've got the list. It's right here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Well, what are we waiting for? Let's take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, that's a lot of pages! It's gonna take forever to get through it all!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We can each take a section. Here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lapouyade... Landois... Jeambel... Horrer...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes, that Horrer guy has a huge scar on his face. He's kinda giving Paimon the creeps.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah, I've met him before. The scar is from an injury he received during a mission. I still remember him joking with me about it. He said any future lover would take one look at him and then lose all interest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did he say anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, I asked if there was someone he was interested in. He said no, and that's where our conversation ended.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It was only later that I learned he really did have someone he liked. He risked everything to escape so he could be with her, but it didn't work. One day, "Father" asked to see him, and well... I never saw him again after that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so that means, The Knave, she...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It may seem cruel, but it's just one of the rules of the House.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Betrayal is not to be taken lightly. We know too many secrets to come and go as we please. So, if you do try to leave, you pay with your life.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A solemn atmosphere descends over the group as you look through the list of names. However, Clervie's name does not seem to be among them.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Her name's not here, huh... Well, that's not too surprising. It doesn't seem like this list is complete. It only contains records dating back around five years.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Let's shift our attention, then. Freminet, were you able to find anything out?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Freminet?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Ah sorry, I was thinking about something.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I managed to talk to quite a few people, but I couldn't help but notice that the atmosphere in the House was a little... strange.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Strange?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Yeah. I mean, I know there have been arguments in the past, times when people haven't gotten along. Chapleau and Filliol are a good example of that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, those are two of the people we met while delivering supplies! Paimon can see how they might not get along. They had very different vibes, and their, um... "interests" seemed to be pretty different as well...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's to be expected, actually. "Father" brought us all here, shared her knowledge with us, taught us how to fight — that's one thing we all share. But, that's also where the similarities end. Not all of us feel the same desire to stay here.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: As members of the House of the Hearth, we're also considered part of the Fatui. And to a lot of people, that's an identity they never asked for.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Certain members get older and realize they want something else for themselves. But, considering the rules of the House... most people would never say that out loud.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: People like Chapleau and Foltz are loyal to "Father" and her vision. They're proud to be part of the Fatui. Filliol and Nanteuil on the other hand... Well, they aren't quite as enthusiastic.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: These kinds of conflicts have always been there. It's not like "Father" is in the dark about any of this.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Well, that's true, but it just feels like things have gotten worse lately. Filliol and the others... It seemed like they were meeting in secret to talk about something.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I can't say for sure, but I think they've met Clervie.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You think she's been inciting them to act out?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: No, not exactly... But, I wouldn't be surprised if she said something to them about "the darkness in the House" and how deep it runs.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: She's told me about it before... experiments being run on children, people being used as pawns on the battlefield without so much as the strength to survive...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: And they just believed all that? Without any evidence?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Clervie's words probably gave them the excuse they were looking for. Whether they actually believe them to be true is secondary.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: *sigh*... This is all because of "Project Stuzha," isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, woah, woah. Hold on a second!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this "Project Stuzha" all about, huh? This is the second time it's come up now!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Sorry, but I'm not sure of the details either.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I only know what "Father" has told us, which is that it's something The Rooster and Regrator have been working on together. Apparently, it has to do with the Fatui's strategic plan for the future.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Because the House of the Hearth was so successful in obtaining the Gnosis, we now have the honor of playing a key role in Project Stuzha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... but isn't that a good thing?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: "Key" role is just another way of saying "dangerous" role. To us, the whole thing is an inconvenience.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: "Father" thinks so too, but she's in no position to refuse. Their plan isn't exactly unreasonable, and they've been funneling the House a lot of funding.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It's just that... We'll lose a lot of members in the process. Participating in the plan... It's an honor in name only. What they're really trying to do is subdue us. The existence of an intelligence organization outside their control makes them feel uneasy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like the Fatui are plotting something big, but given how little Lyney and the others seem to know about it, I probably won't be able to learn much.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I should keep a sharp eye out during any future dealings with the Fatui to see what I can learn.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, super complicated, top-secret Fatui business aside... What does all this have to do with the conflicts you were talking about earlier? Paimon doesn't get the connection...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: External pressure has a way of exacerbating internal strife. You can't overlook the power of fear, either. People are afraid of dying, and that fear is often the impetus for a lot of stupid decisions.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I thought resolving the Clervie situation would make everything go back to normal.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But it looks like things are more complicated than I thought. If we leave Filliol and the others to their own devices, sooner or later, "Father" will be forced to take action.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: We can only focus on one situation at a time, Brother.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You're right. Even if we confront Filliol and the others, it won't do any good. It might even make matters worse. We should focus on Clervie for now.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, it's getting late. We should head back and get some rest. We'll try again first thing tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Lynette, you stick with me this time. Freminet, keep a close eye on Filliol and the others. Make sure they don't do anything they'll regret.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Good work today, everyone. Have a good night, and I'll see you tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn*... Paimon was looking forward to an early night, but she can't sleep at all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you don't think The Knave will be too angry with Lyney and everyone if she finds out about all this, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #She's even scary when she smiles. If she were to actually get angry... *shudder* You have to protect Paimon if that happens, okay {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, in that case, we should just plan on... running away! We'll grab Lyney and the others and, we can make a break for it as fast as we can!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look! Look, over there!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Quick, let's catch up with her before anyone sees!

choices.text: You can just hide behind me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Trusty as ever, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Oh? You decided to stay a little longer? Let's take in the ocean view together then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Clervie!

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: Shh!

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: I opened the window while no one was looking.

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: Look how pretty the outside is...

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: If only I could have more than this.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: You probably think I'm being silly, huh? All this hopeless resisting... It's better to dream of what I could have than try to make it a reality, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Please help us get on the same page here, Clervie. We need you to tell us what you know. Can you do that?

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Sure! Although... after you hear all this, I think you might regret that decision.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Everyone in this family is nothing more than a tool, something to be used and exploited. We're all expendable... including me.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: As long as you're useful, you get to stick around. Lose your value... and you're handed over to The Doctor, experimented on, and given a fate worse than death. I've seen it happen again and again, and I've had enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're saying The Knave did all that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just... That doesn't seem like something she would do. She's scary and all, but it seems like even she has lines she wouldn't cross.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Heh, I knew you wouldn't believe me.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Everyone thinks she's a good person. They all think of her like a real "Mother"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Mother"?

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: But she doesn't deserve that title. She's disgraced it and tarnished it... and if I had things my way, I'd never see her again.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: If only Perrie were here. She'd understand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Perrie... There's that name again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, Paimon's getting a strange feeling...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It almost feels like she's not really "here" with us. Paimon can't tell if she's actually talking to us, or if she's mistaken us for someone else...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Well, in any case, it seems like she really needs someone to talk to. We should keep her company for a little longer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She looks so young, but it seems like she's been through a lot.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: It's getting windy. I should close the window...

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Ooh, look at the moon! Isn't it pretty? ...Hey, wanna hear a secret? I heard that if you look up at the night sky in Snezhnaya, you can see the aurora. It's supposed to be super pretty... even prettier than the moon tonight.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd love to see it.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Perrie and I promised each other, that once we're older, we're gonna go see it together.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: But I can't find her. I'm worried she's also been... No, that wouldn't happen to her. She's special. Mother likes her a lot.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: I should really go talk to Mother, but we just fought. She doesn't want to see me, and I'm too scared to face her.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: What should I do...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Clervie appears lost in thought. She stands there silently and doesn't say another word.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some time, Clervie seems to come back to herself. She gives a weak smile and leaves on her own.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh*... Paimon really doesn't understand what's going on with her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, let's head back. We've got an early morning tomorrow!

choices.text: She's a spirit. It could be anything.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Hmm, where should I start looking...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Clervie, I'd like to take you somewhere. Is that okay with you?

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: Sure! Where are we going?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where's she going? *sigh* If someone sees her, we're toast...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, look! She stopped!
